title: Aggregates over ±inf: NaN
description: A `sum` or `mean` over both infinities is NaN, and `std`, `var` over a group with an infinity are NaN.

`Float32` takes the same generic code in single precision, so a `Float32` sum of inf and -inf is NaN too, on both engines, grouped and not. Nothing checks for the infinities; the Kahan step keeps its error term only while it is finite, so it adds no NaN of its own.

A `sum` of finite values that overflows is `±inf` without raising: `sum` of 1e308 and 1e308 (`Float64`) and of 3e38 and 3e38 (`Float32`, summed in `Float32`) is inf, grouped and not, on both engines. `mean` of the `Float64` pair is inf; `mean` of the `Float32` pair sums in `f64` and is the finite 3.0000000054977558e+38.
The docs are silent on infinities and NaN in `sum`, `mean`, `var` and `std`: a docs gap.
No upstream test pins `inf + (-inf)` or `var` and `std` with an infinity; they may change between versions.

`var`, `std`, `cov` and `corr` of a group holding `+inf` or `-inf` in `x` are NaN (streaming, one thread): no operation of the plan makes the NaN, so it is `nan_creation`'s (the reference raises, D37). An infinity only in `y` leaves `var(x)` finite and makes `cov` and `corr` NaN; a single `inf` alone gives a null sample `var` and a NaN `corr`. Grouped, only the group holding the infinity is NaN.
`quantile_cont` and `median` over values holding both `-inf` and `+inf` give NaN at a fraction between the two infinite neighbours: the NaN is `nan_creation`'s (the reference raises, D37).
reference: `nan_creation`: raise (#257); a statistical aggregate of ±inf raises (`nan_creation`). ST-3 and ST-5 record that Substrait leaves both open.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_polars` runs each expression on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the bounds of the integer width; 0.5, ±2.5, 7, 1e308, ±inf, NaN; NULL), one row at a time, and compares each row with Lean's outcome of the Substrait call under each candidate option (`substrait-check --outcomes`). Observations are Polars programs whose result is recorded as it is. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), Rust crates at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), on macOS arm64.

evidence.note: Polars 2.1.0 (streaming engine, POLARS_MAX_THREADS=1): `quantile(p, 'linear')` of [-inf, +inf] at p = 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 is NaN (-inf at 0.0, +inf at 1.0); of [-inf, 1] it is NaN at 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 and 1 at 1.0; of [-inf, 1, +inf]: NaN at 0.25, 1 at 0.5, +inf at 0.75; of [-inf, -inf, 1]: -inf at 0.25 and 0.5, NaN at 0.75; of [1, +inf]: +inf. `lo + (hi − lo)·w` is NaN wherever `lo` is -inf and `hi` is greater.
